planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade.

directions: Charleston Pink is a seedling selection raised from a garden population in Charleston, Illinois, chosen for soft pink blooms that break from the blue-to-lavender range typical of wild blue phlox. Clumps of narrow evergreen foliage build into a dense mound over several seasons and are topped in mid-spring by loose clusters of fragrant flowers. Because the foliage is prone to powdery mildew in hot, humid summers, give plants good air circulation and avoid overcrowding to keep the mound looking fresh. Light shade with morning sun brings on the most abundant bloom while limiting mildew stress through summer.

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade.

directions: Lemon Slice arose as a streaky sport on a woodland phlox seedling and was stabilized into a foliage cultivar grown as much for its leaves as its flowers. Each small leaf carries a central gold stripe down the green blade, so the low evergreen clump reads as a two-toned groundcover long before bloom. In mid-spring, fragrant light blue flowers rise on short stalks above the variegated mat, briefly covering the foliage. Plant it where the gold striping can be viewed up close, such as a shaded path edge or container, since the leaf pattern is the main seasonal attraction.

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Manita is a North Creek Nursery selection of wild blue phlox grown for its white flowers, each petal marked at the base with a small purple eye that gives the clump a speckled look from a distance. Ground-hugging, evergreen foliage builds a tight mound that stays presentable through winter in milder zones. Flower spikes rise above the foliage in mid-spring carrying a sweet fragrance that draws early pollinators to the shade garden. Keep soil consistently moist and humus-rich, since the mounding habit makes the plant more sensitive to summer drought stress than looser-spreading woodland phlox selections.

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in dappled to partial shade.

directions: Blue Perfume carries medium-blue flowers in loose terminal clusters, part of a series of named color selections bred alongside the white- and lavender-flowered Perfume cultivars of wild blue phlox. It blooms slightly later than many woodland phlox selections, opening from late spring into early summer, and the clump runs a bit larger in both height and spread than compact cultivars like Blue Elf. The lightly hairy stems root where they touch moist soil, letting an established planting slowly knit together into a loose groundcover under high shade. Divide crowded clumps after flowering to keep plants vigorous and reduce the risk of summer dieback.

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Blue Dreams is a European-introduced selection of wild blue phlox valued for pale violet-blue flowers held in loose, slightly fragrant clusters above a bushy, semi-evergreen mound. Trailing stems root at the nodes as they spread, gradually widening the clump into a soft groundcover at the base of shrubs or beneath deciduous trees. Bloom opens in mid-spring and tapers into early summer, a touch later than many wild-collected forms of the species. Consistent moisture through the growing season keeps the narrow, hairy leaves from scorching and supports a fuller second flush of foliage after flowering.

planting.note: Set container plants out after the danger of frost has passed, into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in dappled shade to part sun.

directions: Apple Slices is a Walters Gardens introduction of Indian pink selected for the darkest wine-red tubular flowers yet seen in the species, each bloom tipped with a contrasting yellow throat and held upright above glossy, whorled foliage. It flowers over a long stretch from late spring into early summer and drops spent blooms cleanly rather than leaving dried flowers hanging on the stem. Plants form an expanding clump rather than running by stolons, so clumps stay tidy for years without needing division to control spread. It flowers most heavily with some direct sun, but in the hottest parts of its range benefits from afternoon shade and reliably moist soil to keep foliage from wilting.
